subject: Next steps: POC acceptance criteria & integration responsibilities
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Park <amy@heliosretail.com>; Samir Khan <samir.khan@heliosretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: discovery + proposed POC acceptance criteria

Amy / Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scoped and scheduled. I tried to keep this focused so the team (and procurement/security) can action.

Highlights from the call:
- Primary goal: validate that Redwood reduces end-to-end inference latency for catalog search reranking and lowers per-token cost vs current hosted solution.
- Workload: ~3k queries/day in peak, 80% short queries (<128 tokens), 20% long (>512 tokens) for session-based chat flows.
- Success window: 4-week pilot following a ~2-week spike/proof stage.

Proposed POC acceptance criteria (please confirm / modify):
1) Latency SLO: 95th percentile steady-state latency < 220 ms for short-traffic routing (peak QPS profile).
2) Cost target: >= 30% reduction in per-request inference cost vs your current endpoint (baseline will be the numbers you shared today).
3) Functional parity: Generated reranking output within business tolerance — average NDCG drop <= 0.02 on the seed prompt set.
4) Integration: SDK client for Node/Python running in your staging environment with streaming enabled; end-to-end traceability in Redwood Console.
5) Security: Network isolation and audit logs for all requests during the pilot; SOC2 evidence handshake completed (if required).

Proposed evaluation plan / timeline:
- Day 0-14: Spike (integration + smoke tests) — install SDK, wire up streaming route, run 1k synthetic queries and seed prompt eval set.
- Day 15-42: Pilot (real traffic ramp) — gradually shift 5-25% traffic, collect latency/cost/quality metrics, run nightly evals and automated regression checks.
- Day 43: Acceptance review meeting (pass/fail against criteria above).

Owners / asks (please confirm who on your side will own each):
- Technical lead (SDK + API routes): Samir Khan (Helios) — please confirm.
- Security / compliance point: security@heliosretail.com — please confirm expected evidence and timeline.
- Redwood engineering owner: Neha Kapoor (integration + streaming) and Ben Carter (ops + instrumentation).

Immediate asks from you today:
1) Confirm the acceptance criteria above (or mark changes inline).
2) Confirm Samir as the technical owner and the security contact(s).
3) Share a sandbox API key or test endpoints and a shared Drive link for the test prompt set (if available).

I attached a short scope doc and an API matrix to help your engineer map routes to our SDKs. If the above looks good I’ll schedule a 30-minute engineering kickoff with Samir + Neha + Ben for later this week.

Thanks —

Mateo Alvarez

Thanks — prepping notes from my side for the kickoff and attaching the SDK checklist. High level plan below; I'll bring the checklist to the call (also uploaded to the shared Drive).

Quick technical integration plan (summary):
- SDKs: Node (>=14 LTS) + Python (>=3.9) supported. Official packages: @redwood/inference and redwood_inference.
- Routes:
  * /v1/generate (sync generation)
  * /v1/stream/generate (server-sent events / chunked streaming)
  * /v1/embeddings (batched embeddings)
  * /v1/rerank (optional shortcut for reranking workloads)
- Streaming behavior: SSE events stream tokens as they are generated. Recommend client-side reconnect/backoff and server-side idempotency key for resume.
- Token limits and batching: For this workload we recommend a streaming chunk size of 128 tokens; set max_tokens=512 for long flows. Use continuous batching with a 20ms latency cap for short queries.
- KV cache: If Helios wants session-level history for chat flows, enable remote KV caching with key TTL=30min — reduces repeated context sends.
- Tool/func calling: We support function/tool calling via JSON-schema decorated responses. If you plan to call downstream services from model output, we'll predefine a small set of tool schemas and validate outputs server-side.
- Security: mutual TLS optional for private deployments; for hosted pilot we'll enable IP allowlist + per-key audit logs.

Deliverables for Day 0-14 spike:
1) SDK install + smoke test script (node and python) — repo with example code.
2) Route mapping doc (mapping of Helios endpoints to /v1/* routes).
3) Streaming test harness and load generator for the 1k synthetic queries.
4) Minimal observability dashboard (latency, success/error rate, token counts).

Attachments uploaded: sdk-integration-checklist.md, redwood_poc_api_matrix.xlsx (annotated).

Owner commitments:
- Integration lead: Neha Kapoor (I will take the Spike + streaming integration).
- Ops / instrumentation: Ben Carter (will own dashboards & cost metrics).
- QA / regression harness: Stephanie Nguyen (will own nightly eval runs).

I will also include a short rollback plan: if 95th percentile latency exceeds 350ms for >15 minutes during early pilot ramp, we will throttle traffic back to 5% and switch to a smaller model variant while we investigate kernel/batching configs.

-Neha

Ben
